verdicts.reviewer_notes: Third review. Both review-2 fixes are applied. The 2026-01-01 entry now cites Cal. Const. art. IV sec. 8. I re-fetched it, and (c)(1) reads verbatim: 'a statute enacted at a regular session shall go into effect on January 1 next following a 90-day period from the date of enactment'. Enactment on 29 Sep 2025 plus 90 days is 28 Dec 2025, so the statute took effect 1 January 2026. The summary's last sentence was replaced as required. I re-fetched the leginfo status and bill-text pages. Confirmed: Chapter 138, approved 29 Sep 2025; >10^26 operations; large frontier developer >$500M gross revenue; material framework modifications published within 30 days; 15-day OES incident reporting and 24-hour disclosure for imminent risk; up to $1M per violation, enforced by the AG; CalCompute operative only upon a budget appropriation; no urgency clause. date_correct, status_correct (in_force) and source_tier_correct (both timeline URLs are leginfo, primary) now pass. No duplicate outside content/runs/ (I grepped content/ for SB 53 / sb-53). Reading the bill text closely turned up three wording problems, so claim_matches_source fails. (1) The summary says the law requires 'large developers of frontier models ... to publish safety frameworks and transparency reports, report critical safety incidents, and protect whistleblowers'. The bill text puts only the framework and the internal-use risk summaries on large frontier developers. Sec. 22757.12(c) puts transparency reports on 'a frontier developer'. Incident reporting and the Labor Code 1107.1 whistleblower protections also apply to all frontier developers. Only the anonymous internal process is limited to large developers. The summary narrows the law's scope. (2) The obligation 'Publish a frontier AI framework, updated annually' overstates the duty. The text says 'review and, as appropriate, update its frontier AI framework at least once per year'. (3) The obligation 'Submit quarterly summaries' omits the alternative in the text: 'every three months or pursuant to another reasonable schedule specified by the large frontier developer and communicated in writing to the Office of Emergency Services'.
required_changes: Replace the summary's first sentence with: 'California law on frontier models (trained above 10^26 operations). All frontier developers must publish transparency reports when deploying new or substantially modified frontier models, report critical safety incidents, and observe whistleblower protections. Large frontier developers (over $500 million annual gross revenue) must also publish a frontier AI framework, send internal-use catastrophic risk summaries to the Office of Emergency Services, and provide an anonymous internal reporting process.' Keep the remaining summary sentences unchanged.

Change key obligation 1 to: 'Large frontier developers: publish a frontier AI framework, review it at least once per year and update as appropriate; publish material modifications with a justification within 30 days'.
Change key obligation 2 to: 'Frontier developers: publish a transparency report before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model'.

Change key obligation 4 to: 'Large frontier developers: send OES summaries of catastrophic risk assessments from internal use every three months or on another reasonable schedule communicated to OES in writing'.
Change key obligation 5 to: 'Whistleblower protections for covered employees of frontier developers; large frontier developers must also provide an anonymous internal reporting process'.

verdicts.reviewer_notes: Third review. All three review-2 required changes are applied verbatim. I re-fetched every cited page. leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205: signed 17 May 2024, requirements effective 1 February 2026, which matches the first entry. leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb25b-004: signed 28 August 2025, and the page says 'extends the effective date of the requirements of Senate Bill 24-205 to June 30, 2026'. The revised note matches. leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb26-189: signed 14 May 2026, Chapter 131, and it 'repeals and reenacts' the SB 24-205 provisions as an ADMT framework. The 2026-05-14 note no longer contains litigation text, which matters because this page does not mention X.AI v. Weiser. I checked every key obligation against the SB 26-189 summary. It lists seven consequential-decision areas: education, employment, housing, financial/lending, insurance, health care, and essential government services/public benefits. Developers must provide technical documentation (intended uses, training-data categories, known limitations) starting 1 January 2027, and the page says verbatim 'Developers must notify deployers of material updates or modifications'. Developers and deployers keep records for 3 years. Deployers give notice at the point of interaction and a plain-language description within 30 days of an adverse outcome. Consumers can request their personal data, correction and human review. The AG enforces through the CCPA, with a 60-day cure period ending 1 January 2030. I re-fetched Norton Rose Fulbright for the summary's litigation sentence. It confirms X.AI and the AG filed a joint motion, the court 'granted the Parties' joint motion, temporarily suspending enforcement of the AI Act', and the original effective date was 30 June 2026. The summary marks this sentence as secondary and says the order was not read, which is consistent with the rubric. Status 'amended' fits a repeal-and-reenactment whose new obligations start 1 January 2027. Grep of content/ outside runs/ found no Colorado or SB 24-205/26-189 duplicate. Tone is neutral. Editor follow-up from review 2 still stands: capture the 27 April 2026 order as a separate court-type item citing the Norton Rose Fulbright note, at low or medium confidence.
